items.label: A
items.critique: Plain and well paced, but the route is laid out in surveyor's detail (air shaft, who dug it and why, ladder by the water barrels); Westwood rarely spends three sentences on directions. 'Good luck, my son!' is a nice touch.

items.label: B
items.critique: Breathless exclamations, a missing comma after the appositive, a vague 'reward' and 'tokens of my appreciation': the slightly rough, earnest voice of the campaign.

items.label: C
items.critique: Chatty self-introduction ('[Person]'s the name!', 'put a deal to you'), ellipsis inside the offer and a cheerleading journal ('Bounty accepted!') read like a writer imitating folksiness rather than Nox's plain speech.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'Honestly' as an opener and the jokey journal 'Kill [Person]'s wolves... for good.' are off-register; the thanks line explains the gold's use and flatters the player in a way Westwood does not.

items.label: E
items.critique: Stiff, slightly pompous lawman diction ('I surmise', 'savage scum', 'despicable scoundrel'), double-dash, a concrete sum, and the awkward 'single handedly': unmistakably the campaign's voice.

items.label: F
items.critique: Short, voice-acted panic ('Ooooh, how can this be?') and a functional hand-off to the next person; the journal is plain and object-led as Westwood's are.

items.label: G
items.critique: Ornate exclamatory description ('Roost of the foulest [Group] ever to plague a forge!') and 'nest and all' feel crafted; the terse thanks with 'No doubt the smiths will sleep better' is a writerly flourish.

items.label: H
items.critique: Comic plainness (apples, a foul little urchin, aggravated bats), an item handed over with its use, a petition hook to the next gate, inconsistent capitalisation of Urchin: classic Nox.

items.label: I
items.critique: Hesitant stammer ('Could you... would you burn it out'), a reward routed through a third party, and a journal written as narrated musing ('Maybe there's a bounty for burning it...') are far from Nox's imperative journal style.

items.label: J
items.critique: Exclamation-heavy plea, 'worse than the pox', the request to charm rather than kill, and a formal thanks granting a title and passage: the campaign's shape and register.

tells: Journal entries: Westwood's are short imperatives naming the task and target; the new ones add exclamations, jokey trailing ellipses or narrated speculation.
Ellipses and stammering for effect inside speeches mark the new texts; Westwood favours exclamation marks and double dashes.
Folksy self-introductions and conversational openers ('Honestly', '[Person]'s the name!') are not in Westwood's register, which gets straight to the trouble.
New texts decorate places with ornate epithets or over-detailed directions; Westwood describes just enough to act on.
Westwood's thanks often hand over a concrete next step (an item, a pass, a person to see) or a stiff formal compliment; the new ones add sentimental or witty asides about the aftermath.
Westwood's lines keep small roughnesses (missing commas, inconsistent capitals, odd compounds) that the new texts are too clean to show.
